pitch.label: The outcome, not the attempt
pitch.text: What if an AI team could put a bounty on its model's worst mistake? GradientMine is building that outcome market.

pitch.label: A specific buyer problem
pitch.text: Small model-owning teams pay for engineers and compute without knowing whether the metric will improve. They need a measurable fix, not another experiment.

pitch.label: Define the win
pitch.text: The owner defines the model, baseline, target, evaluator and reward. Bounty Studio makes those terms inspectable. Today's browser draft is explicitly unfunded.

pitch.label: Competing fixes
pitch.text: Independent worker processes submit bounded model updates. A named evaluator compares them on the same held-out examples after the deadline, not on their own claimed scores.

pitch.label: A measured local result
pitch.text: The recorded Digits classifier improves from eighty-four point seven two to ninety-five point two eight percent. That's ten point five six percentage points across three hundred sixty held-out examples.

pitch.label: Verify it yourself
pitch.text: Judges can check fourteen artifact hashes and six digital signatures in their own browser. The evidence is inspectable, not just an impressive number on a slide.

pitch.label: A credible boundary
pitch.text: This is a small, public, budget-limited benchmark. Signatures authenticate evidence, not scientific truth. The evaluator remains trusted.

pitch.label: Why Solana
pitch.text: Solana handles escrow, registered recipients, authorized settlement and refunds. The native Rust program is tested in a local virtual machine. No funded Devnet payout is claimed.

pitch.label: The commercial test
pitch.text: The proposed business is a ten-percent success fee. Next comes testing demand with three to five model-owning design partners. There are no paying customers yet.

pitch.label: The builder
pitch.text: GradientMine is built by Nitish Kapa, founder of Syrava, with graduate training in data science. The next milestone is a real customer choosing to pay for a verified fix.

pitch.label: The proposition
pitch.text: Compute marketplaces sell compute. GradientMine aims to sell measurable improvement. Define the win. Verify the fix.

demo.label: What this demo proves
demo.text: This is GradientMine's working browser experience, captured from the public site. The training results are a recorded local experiment. No wallet connection or payment is being simulated.

demo.label: Draft the outcome
demo.text: Start in Bounty Studio. This support-routing example is illustrative, not customer data. Set the baseline and target, identify the proposed evaluator, and inspect the candidate budget and reward terms.

demo.label: Reject a bad target
demo.text: A target below the baseline is not an improvement. The builder flags the problem instead of accepting a misleading contract. Restoring the target removes that error. The proposed ten-percent fee remains a planning assumption, not billing.

demo.label: Keep the draft honest
demo.text: The export stays blocked until the model and data rights acknowledgement is checked. This demo does not make that declaration for a real customer. The output would be an unfunded local blueprint, not an on-chain bounty.

demo.label: Inspect the real competition
demo.text: Now switch to the recorded experiment. Three real worker processes ran on one machine. One intentionally shuffled its training labels as a negative control. It did not clear the improvement requirement. This is not a caught attacker or three remote operators.

demo.label: Compare on the same holdout
demo.text: The selected candidate reaches ninety-five point two eight percent, from eighty-four point seven two. The gain is ten point five six percentage points on three hundred sixty examples. Its adjusted approximate lower bound is positive. The public benchmark remains reconstructible.

demo.label: Run the evidence check
demo.text: Click Verify recorded evidence. The browser fetches the referenced files, checks their hashes, verifies the expected worker and evaluator signatures, and compares policy and winner references. The result reports fourteen checked artifacts and six signatures.

demo.label: Show a controlled failure
demo.text: Here is a disclosed negative-control test. Only this test browser receives an altered artifact response; the production data is unchanged. Running the same audit now fails the hash check. It does not display a false verification pass.

demo.label: Inspect the signed receipt
demo.text: The evidence inspector exposes the exact receipt, its hash, and the expected signer's verification status. The model passport links the parent, accepted artifact, evaluator, measured improvement and settlement status. Inspectable bytes do not prove the evaluator's scientific claim.

demo.label: Separate scoring from settlement
demo.text: Solana is the economic layer: escrow, recipient registration, authorized settlement, and timeout refunds. Model evaluation stays off-chain. The compiled Rust program has local virtual-machine tests; a funded end-to-end Devnet payout is still a separate milestone.

demo.label: A measurable next step
demo.text: That is the complete prototype story: define the objective, inspect competing fixes, verify the evidence, and keep the settlement boundary explicit. The next proof is a real model owner who prefers paying for the improvement.
